acidity_gerd.title: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) & Acid Indigestion
symptoms: burning sensation in chest after eating spicy food
acid reflux sour taste in mouth after heavy meal
heartburn retrosternal burning when lying down
epigastric burning discomfort regurgitation

feeling hot burning bile coming up throat
stomach acid coming up into esophagus when bending
indigestion with painful burning behind breastbone
hyperacidity post-prandial burning sensation
acidity_gerd.context: Acid reflux occurs when gastric acid flows retrograde across the lower esophageal sphincter, causing mucosal irritation and burning retrosternal sensation.
self_care: Maintain an upright posture for at least 2 hours following meals.
Avoid dietary triggers including citrus fruits, caffeinated beverages, chocolates, and high-fat items.
Elevate the head of your bed by 6 inches during sleep.
Refrain from large volume dinners within 3 hours of reclining.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet once daily
2 teaspoons
otc_regimen.timing: After meals and before bedtime as needed

red_flags: Radiation of chest pain to left arm, neck, or jaw
Difficulty or pain while swallowing (dysphagia/odynophagia)
Vomiting fresh blood or coffee-ground material
Unexplained rapid weight loss
acidity_gerd.referral: Consult a gastroenterologist if symptoms persist beyond 14 days, recur frequently, or fail to respond to proton pump inhibitors.

acute_fever.title: Acute Mild-to-Moderate Febrile Episode
symptoms: high body temperature 101 fahrenheit feeling warm and shivering
fever with chills shivering and mild body aches
temperature spike 100.5 feeling hot feverish fatigue
pyrexia sweating chills malaise and body warmth
running temperature with shivering after rain

feverish feeling chills shivering intermittent sweats
low grade temperature 99 to 101 with tired feeling
sudden onset feverish chills weakness
acute_fever.context: Pyrexia is an immune-mediated elevation of body temperature regulated by hypothalamic prostaglandins in response to endogenous or viral pyrogens.
self_care: Rest in a well-ventilated, temperature-neutral room.
Perform lukewarm water sponging across the forehead and extremities if temperature exceeds 101°F.
Maintain rigorous oral hydration with electrolytes, coconut water, and soups (at least 2.5–3 liters daily).
Wear light, breathable cotton clothing.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet every 6 to 8 hours as needed for temperature > 100°F (Max 3g/day)
otc_regimen.timing: After food with a full glass of water

red_flags: Temperature exceeding 103°F (39.4°C) unresponsive to antipyretics
Rigid stiff neck with altered mental consciousness or confusion
Petechial, purpuric, or non-blanching skin rash
Severe persistent vomiting causing inability to retain fluids
acute_fever.referral: Consult a physician immediately if fever persists beyond 72 hours, drops and rebounds sharply, or presents in immunocompromised individuals.

tension_headache.title: Tension-Type Cephalea & Screen Strain Headache
symptoms: dull band-like ache pressing around temples and forehead
tight pressure squeezing head after long day of computer screen work
bilateral forehead ache tightness around scalp and neck
tension headache stress tight band around skull

scalp tenderness and band-like constriction around head
mild throbbing at temples from eye strain and lack of sleep
tension_headache.context: Tension-type headache results from sustained hypercontraction of pericranial muscles and cervical fascia, often exacerbated by ergonomic screen strain and psychological stress.
self_care: Apply a cold or warm compress across the forehead and posterior neck muscles.
Practice the 20-20-20 screen rule: every 20 minutes look at an object 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Perform gentle cervical spine stretching and shoulder rolls.
Ensure adequate hydration and minimum 7 hours of restorative sleep.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet as a single dose (Max 2 doses/day)
otc_regimen.timing: Post-prandial (strictly with or after meals for ibuprofen)
otc_regimen.duration: Maximum 48 hours to prevent medication overuse headache

red_flags: Sudden explosive thunderclap headache reaching peak intensity in seconds
New onset focal neurological deficits (unilateral numbness, facial drooping, slurred speech)
Headache accompanied by papilledema, visual field loss, or projectile vomiting
Onset after recent head trauma
tension_headache.referral: Schedule an in-person neurological evaluation if headaches occur more than 3 times weekly, progressively worsen, or awaken you from sleep.

common_cold_rhinitis.title: Acute Upper Respiratory Catarrh & Rhinitis
symptoms: runny nose watery eyes sneezing and nasal congestion

congested nostrils mouth breathing due to block and sneezing
acute head cold with clear fluid draining from nose
common_cold_rhinitis.context: Acute rhinitis is a self-limiting viral infection of the nasopharyngeal mucosa leading to hypersecretion of mucus, mucosal edema, and reflex sneezing.
self_care: Inhale steam with plain boiled water or menthol crystals twice daily for 10 minutes.
Perform isotonic saline nasal irrigations or sprays to clear crusting and mucosal allergens.
Drink warm fluids including ginger tea, warm water with lemon, and clear broths.
Use a clean humidified environment.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet once daily at night
2-3 drops into each nostril

red_flags: Stridor, audible wheezing, or marked shortness of breath
High fever persisting beyond day 4 with severe facial bone tenderness
Purulent thick greenish discharge with unilateral maxillary dental pain
Swelling or redness around the eyes
common_cold_rhinitis.referral: Consult an ENT specialist if sinus pressure intensifies beyond 7 days, ear discharge develops, or breathing becomes laboured.

acute_bronchial_cough.title: Acute Tracheobronchial Cough (Dry or Productive)
symptoms: persistent dry tickling cough keeping me awake at night
hacking dry cough throat irritation without phlegm
wet chesty cough with thick white mucus phlegm
productive cough throat clearing mucus in chest
cough fits tickle in trachea barking dry cough
throat tickle causing uncontrollable coughing paroxysms
rattling chest sound with coughing up phlegm
dry irritation in windpipe causing constant hacking
coughing spells worse when lying flat at night
intermittent productive cough following viral illness
acute_bronchial_cough.context: Acute cough is a protective vagal reflex mediated by hypersensitive airway receptors following viral mucosal sloughing, mucosal hypersecretion, or post-nasal drip.
self_care: Consume 1 teaspoon of natural honey with warm water or herbal infusion (not in infants < 1 year).
Maintain continuous humidification of ambient sleeping quarters.
Avoid aerosolized irritants, tobacco smoke, and sudden cold air exposure.
Stay adequately hydrated to lower phlegm viscosity.

otc_regimen.molecule: Dextromethorphan (Dry Cough) OR Ambroxol + Guaifenesin (Wet Cough)
otc_regimen.dosage: 5-10ml measured with oral dosing cup

red_flags: Hemoptysis (expectorating streaks of fresh blood or rusty sputum)
Resting respiratory rate > 24 breaths/min with oxygen saturation < 94%
Audible musical wheezing with intercostal retractions
Significant pleuritic chest pain aggravated by deep inspiration
acute_bronchial_cough.referral: Seek an urgent pulmonology consult if cough lingers longer than 3 weeks, produces colored purulent sputum with fever, or coexists with asthma/COPD.

generalized_pain_myalgia.title: Acute Musculoskeletal Strain & Generalized Myalgia

sore muscles stiffness in back and limbs after heavy lifting

dull aching in calf muscles and thighs after unaccustomed exercise
musculoskeletal soreness tender muscle knots in upper back
body fatigue aching all over after strenuous manual labour
mild lower lumbar muscular spasm after twisting
generalized_pain_myalgia.context: Myalgia typically stems from microscopic structural disruptions of myofibers following eccentric mechanical loading, localized lactic acid accumulation, or viral immune responses.
self_care: Practice the R.I.C.E. protocol (Rest, Ice for first 48h, Compression, Elevation) for localized sprains.
Apply warm compresses or heating pads after 48 hours to promote microvascular hyperemia.
Engage in non-ballistic gentle mobility stretches.
Avoid heavy spinal axial loading until acute spasm abates.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 oral tablet every 8 hours PRN; apply gel gently 3 times daily without vigorous friction

red_flags: Bowel or bladder incontinence with saddle anesthesia (Cauda Equina emergency)
Inability to bear any weight on the affected limb with visible osseous deformity
Erythematous, hot, markedly swollen joint suggesting septic arthritis
Severe progressive neurological weakness (foot drop, hand grip loss)
generalized_pain_myalgia.referral: Consult an orthopedic specialist or physiotherapist if pain does not resolve within 7 days, radiates below the knee, or causes progressive weakness.

ligament_sprain_cramp.title: Acute Ligament Sprain, Tendon Strain & Muscle Cramps
symptoms: twisted ankle ligament sprain painful weight bearing
sprained ankle swollen bruised ligament pain walking

painful muscle spasm and tendon strain after twisting
swollen tender ankle after stepping on uneven ground
hamstring pull strain sharp sudden muscle pain during run
muscle twitching cramp localized fasciculation fatigue
ligament_sprain_cramp.context: Ligament sprains involve stretching or partial tearing of joint-stabilizing collagenous fibers, while muscle cramps stem from localized ionic depletion, neuromuscular hyper-excitability, or mechanical overload.
self_care: Immobilize the joint and avoid painful weight bearing during the initial 48 hours.
Apply crushed ice packs wrapped in a cloth for 15-20 minutes every 3-4 hours.
Apply an elastic crepe compression bandage firmly but without restricting peripheral arterial pulses.
Elevate the injured limb above heart level whenever sitting or lying down.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet every 8 hours PRN for inflammatory pain
1 tablet / sachet daily for cramping

red_flags: Immediate inability to take four steps both immediately after the injury and in the examination room (Ottawa Ankle Rules)
Severe localized osseous tenderness over the posterior edge or tip of lateral/medial malleolus
Rapid massive joint effusion (hemarthrosis) or gross angular limb deformity
Cold, pale, pulseless foot or severe numbness in distal toes
ligament_sprain_cramp.referral: Seek orthopedic evaluation and radiography (X-ray) if you cannot bear weight, or if joint instability and severe swelling persist beyond 4 days.

allergic_dermatitis_urticaria.title: Allergic Rhinitis, Pruritus & Urticarial Wheals
symptoms: itchy red hives raised welts on skin with intense itching
allergic skin rash itching red spots after dust or pollen exposure

pruritic erythematous plaques triggered by pet dander
allergic_dermatitis_urticaria.context: Urticaria and allergic pruritus occur due to mast cell degranulation releasing histamine and leukotrienes, inducing dermal capillary vasodilation and localized interstitial edema.
self_care: Apply cool, moist compresses or colloidal oatmeal lotion to soothe inflamed skin.
Take lukewarm showers using hypoallergenic, fragrance-free syndet cleansing bars.
Wear loose-fitting, soft natural cotton clothing to minimize mechanical friction.
Refrain from scratching to prevent secondary bacterial impetiginization.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet once daily at night
Topical application over affected areas
otc_regimen.timing: Apply a thin film 2 to 3 times daily

red_flags: Angioedema of the tongue, uvula, lips, or periorbital tissues
Feeling of throat tightness, hoarse voice, or difficulty swallowing
Stridor, wheezing, lightheadedness, or acute hypotension (Anaphylaxis)
Rapidly progressing bullae or mucosal desquamation (SJS/TEN)
allergic_dermatitis_urticaria.referral: Seek emergency medical care immediately if swelling of the face/throat occurs. Consult an allergist/dermatologist if hives recur for more than 6 weeks.

acute_gastroenteritis_diarrhea.title: Acute Non-Invasive Gastroenteritis & Osmotic Diarrhea

mild traveler diarrhea without blood or high fever
watery stool frequency increased with dry mouth and thirst
hyperactive bowel sounds with sudden loose stools
acute_gastroenteritis_diarrhea.context: Acute infectious or foodborne diarrhea involves hypersecretion of electrolytes and blunted mucosal fluid absorption across enterocytes, leading to potential dehydration.
self_care: Initiate aggressive oral rehydration solution (WHO-ORS) therapy: 200–300ml after every loose stool.
Follow the modified BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice congee, Applesauce, Toast, Boiled potatoes).
Avoid lactose/dairy products, high-sugar fruit juices, alcohol, and spicy greasy meals.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before food handling.

otc_regimen.molecule: WHO Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) + Zinc Gluconate 20mg
otc_regimen.dosage: Dissolve 1 sachet in exactly 1 liter clean drinking water; sip regularly throughout the day
otc_regimen.timing: Ad libitum after each loose bowel movement

otc_regimen.molecule: Probiotic Spores (Bacillus clausii or Saccharomyces boulardii)
otc_regimen.dosage: 1 mini-bottle or sachet twice daily

red_flags: Presence of macroscopic red blood or black tarry melena in stools
Signs of severe dehydration: sunken eyes, skin tenting, lethargy, no urine for > 8 hours
High fever (> 102°F) with intense localized abdominal rebound tenderness
Intractable vomiting preventing any oral fluid intake
acute_gastroenteritis_diarrhea.referral: Consult a physician promptly if diarrhea continues beyond 48 hours, develops bloody dysentery, or manifests in elderly or diabetic individuals.

acute_emesis_nausea.title: Acute Functional Nausea, Emesis & Gastric Upset
symptoms: severe nausea vomiting and food poisoning queasiness

acute_emesis_nausea.context: Nausea is regulated via afferent vagal stimulation of the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) and vomiting center in the medulla oblongata, mediated by dopamine D2 and 5-HT3 receptors.
self_care: Sip clear, cold, or room-temperature liquids in tiny quantities (1-2 tablespoons every 10 minutes).
Consume mild ginger infusions or chew crystallized ginger.
Rest in an elevated semi-fowler position; avoid lying completely flat immediately after drinking.
Avoid strong culinary aromas, greasy foods, and overly sweet liquids.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet (Max 3 tablets in 24 hours)
otc_regimen.duration: Short-term use up to 48 hours only

red_flags: Projectile vomiting or vomiting containing hematin (coffee-ground emesis)
Severe localized pain in right lower quadrant (McBurney point) or epigastrium
Concomitant stiff neck, photophobia, or sudden confusion
Complete inability to retain oral fluids for more than 12 hours
acute_emesis_nausea.referral: Seek immediate medical consultation if vomiting is intractable, accompanied by severe abdominal distension, or follows head injury.

cardiovascular_chest_emergency.title: Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) / Cardiac Emergency
symptoms: crushing chest pain radiating to left arm shoulder jaw with cold sweats
heavy pressure on chest like an elephant sitting on my sternum diaphoresis
acute squeezing retrosternal chest pain shortness of breath dizziness
severe chest tightness radiating to jaw left arm sweating profusely

severe central chest pain with profuse cold sweating and syncope feeling

acute cardiac chest pain breathless pale and clammy
cardiovascular_chest_emergency.context: Crushing retrosternal chest pain with radiation and diaphoresis is a hallmark of acute myocardial ischemia or coronary arterial occlusion requiring emergent revascularization.
self_care: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (112 / 911 / LOCAL AMBULANCE) IMMEDIATELY.
Cease all physical activity and sit in a comfortable resting position on the floor or chair.
Loosen all tight clothing around the neck and chest.
Do NOT attempt to drive yourself to the hospital.

otc_regimen.molecule: Aspirin 300mg (Dispersible/Chewable) - ONLY if advised by emergency dispatch and no allergy
otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet chewed thoroughly immediately
otc_regimen.timing: STAT emergency dose while awaiting ambulance

red_flags: Crushing chest pressure lasting > 5 minutes
Radiation to left shoulder, arm, jaw, neck, or interscapular back
Diaphoresis (drenching cold sweat), syncope, or profound dyspnea
Hypotension, cyanosis, or gray pallor
cardiovascular_chest_emergency.referral: EMERGENCY: Proceed to the nearest cardiac catheterization / emergency resuscitation facility immediately. Call emergency emergency medical services without delay.

neurological_stroke_emergency.title: Suspected Acute Cerebrovascular Event / Stroke
symptoms: sudden facial drooping slurred speech weakness in right arm cannot raise arm
loss of speech facial droop right side body paralysis sudden numbness

neurological_stroke_emergency.context: Acute focal neurological deficit (FAST criteria) signifies acute focal cerebral ischemia or intracranial hemorrhage demanding urgent neuroimaging and thrombolysis within the therapeutic window.
self_care: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (112 / 911) IMMEDIATELY.
Record the EXACT time the symptoms first appeared (Time of Onset).
Keep the patient lying flat on their side (recovery position) to prevent aspiration.
Do NOT administer any oral fluids, food, or aspirin until imaging rules out hemorrhage.
red_flags: Face: One side of the face droops when smiling
Arms: One arm drifts downward when both arms are extended forward
Speech: Slurred, incomprehensible, or absent speech
Time: Critical time window (thrombolysis within 4.5 hours)
neurological_stroke_emergency.referral: CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Transport immediately to a designated Comprehensive Stroke Center for urgent non-contrast head CT and emergency revascularization.

acute_constipation.context: Functional constipation arises from delayed colonic transit and excessive water reabsorption across the colon, commonly aggravated by low dietary fiber, sedentary habits, or dehydration.
self_care: Increase daily soluble and insoluble dietary fiber to 25–30g (whole grains, oats, prunes, psyllium, leafy greens).
Drink at least 2.5 to 3 liters of water across the day, especially a glass of warm water upon waking.
Engage in 30 minutes of aerobic physical movement or brisk walking daily.
Do not ignore or suppress the gastrocolic defecation urge after breakfast.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 to 2 tablespoons in a full glass (250ml) of lukewarm water
otc_regimen.timing: At bedtime, followed immediately by another full glass of water

otc_regimen.dosage: 15ml once daily

red_flags: Complete obstipation with inability to pass flatus and progressive vomiting (bowel obstruction)
Unexplained hematochezia (bright red blood coating or mixed in stool)
New onset constipation in patients over 50 years with involuntary weight loss
Severe unrelenting colic with tense abdominal distension
acute_constipation.referral: Consult a physician if laxatives are required for more than 7 days continuously or if alternating constipation and diarrhea occurs.

acute_pharyngitis_sore_throat.context: Pharyngitis is inflammation of the mucosal lining of the posterior pharynx, commonly triggered by respiratory viruses (adenovirus, rhinovirus) leading to local vascular congestion and sensory nerve irritation.
self_care: Perform warm salt water gargles (1/2 teaspoon table salt in 200ml warm water) 3 to 4 times daily.
Sip soothing warm fluids such as chamomile tea, warm water with turmeric and honey.
Use a cool-mist room humidifier to keep mucosal membranes lubricated.
Rest your vocal cords and avoid whispering, clearing your throat violently, or smoking.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 lozenge dissolved slowly in the mouth every 3 to 4 hours (Max 8/day)
otc_regimen.timing: Between meals as needed for soothing

otc_regimen.dosage: Dilute 1:1 with warm water and gargle for 30 seconds

red_flags: Inability to swallow even saliva with drooling (trismus / peritonsillar quinsy)
Difficulty breathing, inspiratory stridor, or cyanosis (epiglottitis)
High fever with exudative white patches on tonsils and tender anterior cervical lymph nodes
Inability to fully open the mouth
acute_pharyngitis_sore_throat.referral: Consult an ENT physician if throat pain is strictly unilateral, accompanied by high fever without cough (Centor criteria for Strep), or persists beyond 5 days.

aphthous_stomatitis.title: Recurrent Minor Aphthous Stomatitis & Mouth Ulcers

aphthous_stomatitis.context: Aphthous ulcers are painful non-keratinized mucosal erosions characterized by local immune-mediated T-cell destruction, often provoked by minor local trauma, stress, or micronutrient deficiencies.
self_care: Avoid spicy, acidic, citrus, sharp, and very salty foods that provoke severe burning.
Use an ultra-soft bristle toothbrush and avoid sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS)-containing toothpastes.
Rinse the mouth gently with warm salt water after meals.
Ensure adequate dietary intake of B-complex vitamins, zinc, and iron.

otc_regimen.dosage: Apply a pea-sized amount with clean fingertip over the ulcer
otc_regimen.timing: 3 to 4 times daily, 15 minutes before food intake

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 capsule daily

red_flags: Non-healing oral ulcer persisting for greater than 3 weeks (rule out malignancy)
Extremely large (> 1cm) major aphthae with irregular margins and tissue scarring
Ulcers accompanied by genital lesions, uveitis, or joint pain (Behçet syndrome)
Constitutional symptoms including high fever, night sweats, and marked lymphadenopathy
aphthous_stomatitis.referral: Consult a dental surgeon or oral pathologist if any oral lesion does not re-epithelialize within 21 days or recurs with high frequency.

odontalgia_toothache.title: Dental Caries Associated Odontalgia & Gingival Discomfort

odontalgia_toothache.context: Odontogenic pain results from bacterial demineralization of enamel exposing dentinal tubules or causing inflammation of the neurovascular dental pulp (pulpitis).
self_care: Rinse gently with warm salt water to dislodge impacted food particles from the cavity.
Avoid extreme temperatures in foods and beverages (neither freezing nor boiling hot).
Never place an undiluted aspirin or tablet directly against the gum tissue (causes chemical burns).
Maintain meticulous gentle flossing around the affected tooth.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet every 8 hours as needed
otc_regimen.duration: Maximum 48 hours while awaiting dental appointment

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 drop applied on a tiny sterile cotton pellet directly onto the cavity

red_flags: Facial or submandibular swelling with difficulty swallowing or breathing (Ludwig angina)
Spreading redness, trismus (inability to open jaw > 2 fingers)
High fever, chills, and purulent fluctuant drainage from the gum
Swelling extending up towards the orbit/eye
odontalgia_toothache.referral: MANDATORY DENTAL CONSULTATION: Over-the-counter analgesics only provide temporary symptomatic suppression; a formal dental examination and definitive restoration/root canal therapy is required.

tinea_fungal_infection.title: Superficial Cutaneous Dermatomycosis (Tinea / Ringworm)
symptoms: circular itchy red ring rash on inner thighs and groin
ringworm itchy spreading ring with raised border on body
fungal skin infection itchy scaling circular patches

tinea_fungal_infection.context: Tinea is a superficial dermatophyte infection (Trichophyton, Microsporum) that metabolizes keratin in the stratum corneum, thriving in warm, occluded, moist body areas.
self_care: Keep the affected skin thoroughly clean and dry; pat dry with a dedicated clean towel (do not share towels).
Wear loose, breathable cotton undergarments and change them daily.
Do NOT apply topical steroid creams (e.g. betamethasone/clobetasol) which aggravate fungal proliferation (tinea incognito).
Avoid synthetic, tight-fitting clothing and footwear.

otc_regimen.dosage: Apply a thin layer covering the lesion plus a 2cm healthy border
otc_regimen.timing: Twice daily on clean, dry skin
otc_regimen.duration: Continue for a full 2 to 3 weeks (at least 1 week after visible clearance)

otc_regimen.dosage: Dust into skin folds, socks, and undergarments

red_flags: Rapid secondary bacterial infection with purulent oozing, honey-colored crusts, and warm cellulitis
Extensive involvement of the facial skin, palms, soles, or diffuse erythroderma
Involvement of immunocompromised, transplant, or advanced diabetic patients
Failure of lesions to improve after 2 weeks of compliant topical therapy
tinea_fungal_infection.referral: Consult a dermatologist if the rash does not respond to topical therapy, involves fingernails/toenails (onychomycosis), or requires systemic oral antifungal evaluation.

asthenopia_dry_eyes.title: Computer Vision Syndrome & Evaporative Tear Deficiency
symptoms: dry gritty eyes burning sensation after staring at screens
tired burning eyes red gritty feeling like sand in eyes
eye strain blurred vision towards evening after computer work
dry itchy eyes watering paradoxically tired heavy eyelids
gritty sandy feeling in eyes burning screen fatigue

sandy gritty eyes feeling dry and tired under air conditioning
blurring of vision after 8 hours of coding with dry burning eyes
asthenopia_dry_eyes.context: Prolonged digital display use decreases spontaneous blink rate by up to 60%, destabilizing the precorneal tear film lipid layer and inducing evaporative ocular surface microtrauma.
self_care: Strictly follow the 20-20-20 rule: look away every 20 minutes at an object 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Position computer monitors slightly below eye level (15–20 degrees) to minimize exposed ocular surface area.
Avoid direct airflow from fans, air conditioners, or heaters pointed directly at the face.
Remember to take voluntary, complete, firm blinks frequently.

otc_regimen.molecule: Carboxymethylcellulose 0.5% OR Sodium Hyaluronate 0.1% Lubricant Eye Drops
otc_regimen.dosage: 1 to 2 drops into the lower conjunctival sac of each eye
otc_regimen.timing: 3 to 4 times daily as needed for dry ocular comfort

red_flags: Severe deep ocular pain with nausea and rainbow halos around lights (acute angle closure)
Sudden loss of visual acuity or severe persistent blurred vision
Copious purulent discharge gluing eyelids together in the morning (bacterial conjunctivitis)
Corneal ulceration or visible cloudy white spots on the cornea
asthenopia_dry_eyes.referral: Schedule a formal ophthalmological slit-lamp examination if dry eye symptoms persist, worsen despite lubricants, or impair daily visual tasks.

meteorism_bloating.title: Functional Intestinal Meteorism & Gaseous Distension
symptoms: excessive gas flatulence stomach feeling bloated and tight like balloon
gassy bloated belly loud rumbling trapped intestinal gas
abdominal distension burping gas pains relieved by passing wind
feeling very full and bloated with gas cramps after meals
trapped gas in abdomen tight distended stomach loud gurgling
constant belching and flatulence with uncomfortable abdominal bloating
tight inflated feeling in gut with crampy gas discomfort
stomach swelling like a balloon with loud intestinal rumbling
bloated belly after beans and lentils with excessive flatus
cramping abdominal discomfort relieved immediately upon passing flatus
meteorism_bloating.context: Intestinal meteorism arises from microbial fermentation of poorly absorbed oligosaccharides (FODMAPs) or aerophagia, generating excessive hydrogen and methane in the bowel lumen.
self_care: Eat slowly and chew food thoroughly; avoid swallowing air by drinking through straws or talking while chewing.
Temporarily reduce high-fermentation foods (carbonated sodas, beans, cabbage, artificial polyol sweeteners).
Take a gentle 15-minute walk following heavy meals to stimulate gastrointestinal peristalsis.
Sip warm herbal infusions of peppermint, fennel seeds, or ginger.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 chewable tablet chewed thoroughly
otc_regimen.timing: After meals and at bedtime as needed

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 capsule with the first bite of gas-producing meals

red_flags: Progressive severe abdominal distension with intractable vomiting and obstipation (obstruction)
Unexplained rapid weight loss, anemia, or anorexia
Persistent nocturnal abdominal pain awakening you from sleep
Fecal blood or tarry black stools
meteorism_bloating.referral: Consult a gastroenterologist if bloating is chronic (> 4 weeks), progressively worsening, or accompanied by alterations in bowel frequency.

heat_exhaustion_dehydration.title: Acute Thermal Strain & Exertional Dehydration
symptoms: dizzy weak thirsty sweating heavily after being out in hot sun
heat exhaustion dizzy headache extreme thirst dark yellow urine
fatigue dizziness after working in heat faint feeling dehydrated
feeling faint weak profuse sweating dry lips muscle cramps in heat
excessive sweating thirst dizziness heat weakness after outdoor walking
hot climate fatigue with severe thirst and postural lightheadedness
cramping calves and dizziness after sports under hot afternoon sun
dark amber urine extreme thirst and weak legs after heat exposure
lightheadedness upon standing up after sweating in hot humid weather
dehydration headache and dry mouth after prolonged sun exposure
heat_exhaustion_dehydration.context: Heat exhaustion results from excessive dermal fluid and electrolyte depletion via sweating under thermal stress without adequate salt and water replacement.
self_care: Move immediately to a cool, air-conditioned, or shaded environment.
Lie down with feet slightly elevated above heart level.
Loosen or remove tight, heavy garments.
Apply cool wet cloths to the neck, axillae, and groin; fan the skin actively.

otc_regimen.dosage: Dissolve 1 sachet in exactly 1 liter of cool drinking water; drink 500ml over the first hour, then sip steadily
otc_regimen.duration: Until thirst subsides and urine turns pale straw colored

red_flags: Body temperature exceeding 104°F (40°C) with hot, red, dry skin (HEAT STROKE - MEDICAL EMERGENCY)
Altered mental status, delirium, confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness
Inability to tolerate oral fluids due to persistent vomiting
Rapid, bounding pulse transitioning to weak thready hypotension
heat_exhaustion_dehydration.referral: EMERGENCY: If mental status is altered or skin is hot and dry, immediately activate emergency services (112 / 911). Heat stroke has high mortality without rapid active cooling.

minor_dermal_burns.title: Superficial First-Degree Thermal Burn & Minor Scald
symptoms: minor burn on finger from hot cooking oil red stinging skin
small superficial scald on hand from boiling water red painful
hot pan burn on palm red tender skin without big blisters
finger burned on hot iron stinging red minor burn
scalded hand with hot tea redness and burning sensation
superficial kitchen burn on forearm painful erythematous skin
red tender burning spot on skin after accidental steam contact
small hot oil splash on hand stinging red without deep tissue loss
minor thermal burn redness and local pain from hot stove
surface scald from hot soup on finger painful and red
minor_dermal_burns.context: First-degree burns involve localized thermal injury restricted to the epidermal layer, presenting with erythema, capillary dilatation, and intense pain due to exposed cutaneous nerve endings.
self_care: IMMEDIATELY cool the burn under gently running cool (not freezing) tap water for 15 to 20 minutes.
Do NOT apply ice, iced water, butter, toothpaste, or oil (ice causes localized frostbite and tissue ischemia).
Do NOT puncture, squeeze, or de-roof any intact blisters.
Cover the area loosely with a sterile, non-adherent dressing.

otc_regimen.molecule: Silver Sulfadiazine 1% Cream OR Povidone-Iodine 5% Ointment
otc_regimen.dosage: Apply a sterile 1-2mm layer over the cooled burn area
otc_regimen.timing: Once or twice daily under sterile non-stick gauze

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet every 8 hours PRN for burn pain

red_flags: Burn area larger than the palm of the patient's hand
Burns involving critical structures: face, eyes, hands, joints, feet, or perineum
Full-thickness injury: leathery, white, blackened, or painless charred skin (Third-degree)
Chemical or electrical burns (require mandatory hospital observation)
minor_dermal_burns.referral: Proceed immediately to a hospital burn center or emergency room if burns are extensive, circumferential, involve children, or show purulent signs of infection.

motion_sickness_kinetosis.title: Vestibular Kinetosis & Motion Sickness
symptoms: nausea and dizziness when traveling in car hills or bus motion sickness
car sickness nausea vomiting during long road trips in ghats
seasickness motion sickness queasy stomach during boat ferry ride
travel sickness dizziness cold sweating urge to vomit in moving vehicle
nauseous and dizzy in moving car looking at road turns
vertigo and stomach queasiness during flight turbulence or road turns
car travel nausea cold clammy forehead and vomiting feeling
motion sickness headache and dizziness in backseat of car
motion induced vomiting sensation on winding mountain roads
air sickness dizziness and gastric churning during flight
motion_sickness_kinetosis.context: Motion sickness arises from sensory mismatch between visual vestibular proprioceptive signals entering the central nervous system during passive locomotion.
self_care: Sit in the front passenger seat of cars or near the wing section in airplanes.
Focus your gaze straight ahead on the distant horizon; avoid reading books or looking at screens.
Ensure adequate ventilation with cool, fresh air.
Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy meals immediately prior to and during travel.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet taken orally
otc_regimen.timing: Strictly 30 to 60 minutes BEFORE commencing travel journey
otc_regimen.duration: Repeat every 8 hours only if journey continues

red_flags: Persistent spinning vertigo that does NOT cease hours after travel ends
Sudden unilateral sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness
Focal neurological signs: ataxia, diplopia, dysarthria, or extremity weakness
Severe unrelenting vomiting resulting in hemodynamic instability
motion_sickness_kinetosis.referral: Consult a neurologist or neurotologist if vertigo occurs spontaneously at rest, is accompanied by hearing loss, or fails to resolve.

sleep_onset_insomnia.title: Acute Situational Sleep-Onset Insomnia
symptoms: trouble falling asleep tossing and turning in bed racing thoughts
cannot fall asleep insomnia lying awake for hours anxiety
difficulty initiating sleep waking up repeatedly tired morning
sleeplessness tossing in bed for hours cannot shut mind off

stress induced sleeplessness tired but wired feeling in bed
sleep_onset_insomnia.context: Acute insomnia is characterized by cortical hyperarousal, increased nocturnal autonomic activation, and disruption of circadian melatonin signaling, frequently provoked by acute life stress or blue-light exposure.
self_care: Practice strict digital hygiene: power down all smartphones, tablets, and LED displays 60 minutes prior to bedtime.
Ensure the bedroom is pitch-dark, quiet, and cool (approx. 18–20°C).
Follow the 20-minute stimulus control rule: if still awake after 20 minutes, get out of bed, go to a dim room, read a physical book, and return only when sleepy.
Eliminate caffeine intake after 2:00 PM.

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet orally
otc_regimen.duration: Short-term use up to 7 to 10 days

red_flags: Loud irregular snoring punctuated by witnessed apneas, gasping, and morning headaches (Obstructive Sleep Apnea)
Insomnia accompanied by severe depressive thoughts, self-harm ideation, or manic episodes
Restless legs syndrome with unbearable crawling sensations relieved only by movement
Chronic unremitting insomnia lasting > 3 months
sleep_onset_insomnia.referral: Consult a sleep specialist or psychiatrist if sleeplessness persists beyond 4 weeks, significantly impairs daytime occupational functioning, or coexists with mood disorders.

impacted_cerumen_ear.title: Impacted Cerumen & Non-Infectious Aural Fullness
symptoms: ear feels blocked muffled hearing wax buildup in ear canal
ear fullness sensation like cotton plugged in ear dull hearing
earwax blockage muffled ear sound after bathing or swimming
plugged feeling in ear with mild itchiness and hardened wax
ear plugged with wax cannot hear clearly out of one ear

hardened earwax obstruction causing decreased hearing

ear itching and fullness from excessive dry wax accumulation
cotton-bud pushed wax deep into ear causing muffled blockage
impacted_cerumen_ear.context: Impacted cerumen occurs when physiological epithelial migration fails or when foreign objects (cotton swabs) mechanically compact glandular secretions against the tympanic membrane.
self_care: NEVER insert cotton buds, bobby pins, or sharp instruments into the external auditory meatus (causes tympanic perforation and canal lacerations).
Wipe the external pinna gently with a soft damp cloth.
Keep the ear canal dry during showering by placing a cotton ball lightly coated with petroleum jelly at the outer meatus.
Avoid forceful ear syringing without prior otoscopic examination.

otc_regimen.dosage: 3 to 4 drops instilled into the affected ear with head tilted for 5 minutes
otc_regimen.duration: 3 to 5 days to soften wax prior to natural expulsion

red_flags: Purulent, foul-smelling, or bloody otorrhea draining from the canal
Severe excruciating otalgia radiating to temporomandibular joint or mastoid bone
Acute vertigo, severe dizziness, or facial weakness
History of known tympanic membrane perforation or tympanostomy tubes
impacted_cerumen_ear.referral: Consult an ENT specialist for professional micro-suction or gentle syringing if wax does not clear in 5 days or if pain/discharge supervenes.

acne_vulgaris.title: Mild-to-Moderate Inflammatory Acne Vulgaris
symptoms: pimples on face red bumps with whiteheads on forehead and chin
acne breakout pustules and blackheads on oily cheeks
inflammatory pimples red tender facial spots during stress
facial acne bumps oily skin clogged pores on nose and forehead

clogged pores with blackheads and pustular acne on oily face
recurrent acne breakouts with tender inflamed red papules
stubborn pimples and whiteheads across T-zone of face
comedones and inflammatory red bumps on cheeks
skin breakout with oily complexion and painful tender spots
acne_vulgaris.context: Acne vulgaris is a multifactorial disorder of the pilosebaceous unit driven by follicular hyperkeratinization, Cutibacterium acnes colonization, androgenic sebum oversecretion, and localized inflammation.
self_care: Cleanse the face twice daily using a gentle foaming cleanser containing 1–2% salicylic acid.
Do NOT pop, squeeze, or manually pick at pimples (induces deep dermis scarring and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation).
Use strictly non-comedogenic, oil-free moisturizers and broad-spectrum gel sunscreens.
Wash pillowcases and phone screens regularly to minimize bacterial transfer.

otc_regimen.molecule: Benzoyl Peroxide 2.5% Gel OR Clindamycin 1% Topical Gel
otc_regimen.dosage: Apply a thin film as spot treatment directly on active inflammatory papules
otc_regimen.timing: Once daily at night on clean, dry skin
otc_regimen.duration: 4 to 6 weeks for visible follicular clearing

red_flags: Deep, painful, fluctuant cystic nodules forming interconnecting sinus tracts (Acne Conglobata)
Systemic symptoms including acute fever, joint aches, and ulcerating lesions (Acne Fulminans)
Extensive hypertrophic or keloidal scarring developing across the jawline and back
Sudden severe virilization in females (hirsutism, deepening voice, irregular menses)
acne_vulgaris.referral: Consult a dermatologist if inflammatory lesions fail to improve after 6 weeks, leave residual deep pitted scars, or require oral isotretinoin evaluation.

mild_dysuria.title: Mild Lower Urinary Tract Irritation & Early Dysuria
symptoms: burning sensation when passing urine mild irritation in urinary passage
stinging burning during urination needing to pee frequently in small drops
mild dysuria burning sensation at end of urination slightly cloudy
urinary frequency with stinging burning feeling in urethra
mild burning while urinating drinking less water discomfort
urethral stinging upon passing urine without high fever
burning micturition with frequent urge to empty bladder
concentrated dark urine with painful stinging during urination
discomfort in lower abdomen with burning sensation when peeing
frequent visits to bathroom with stinging urethral irritation
mild_dysuria.context: Mild dysuria reflects urothelial mucosal inflammation, frequently secondary to concentrated acidic urine, minor ascending bacterial colonization (E. coli), or local urethral irritation.
self_care: Increase fluid intake immediately: drink 3 to 3.5 liters of clean water and tender coconut water throughout the day.
Do not hold urine; void frequently to mechanically flush bacteria out of the urinary tract.
Maintain strict hygiene: wipe strictly from front to back after voiding in females.
Avoid bladder irritants including coffee, strong tea, alcohol, and spicy condiments.

otc_regimen.dosage: 2 teaspoons (10ml) diluted in a full glass of drinking water
otc_regimen.duration: Up to 3 days for symptomatic relief of burning

red_flags: High spiking fever with shaking chills and rigors
Unilateral flank/back pain over costovertebral angle (suspected acute pyelonephritis)
Frank macroscopic hematuria (visible blood or blood clots in urine)
New onset urinary incontinence or complete inability to pass urine (acute urinary retention)
mild_dysuria.referral: MANDATORY PHYSICIAN CONSULTATION: Schedule a formal urinalysis (urine routine & microscopy + culture sensitivity). If symptoms persist beyond 48 hours or if you are pregnant/male/diabetic, antibiotic therapy requires a licensed doctor prescription.

solar_erythema_sunburn.title: Actinic Erythema (Sunburn) & Heat Rash (Miliaria)
symptoms: sunburn on shoulders red hot skin peeling after beach vacation
red painful sunburn after staying in hot sun without sunscreen
prickly heat rash tiny itchy red bumps in neck and back sweating
miliaria rubra heat rash itching stinging bumps in sweaty areas
painful hot red skin peeling from sun exposure on beach
sunburnt arms and back red inflamed skin tender to shirt contact
prickly stinging heat bumps on chest and shoulders in humid weather
acute solar erythema with warm hypersensitive skin after trekking
itchy red sweat bumps around collarbone and inner elbows
erythematous hot skin with tight burning sensation after sunburn
solar_erythema_sunburn.context: Sunburn is acute UV-B mediated keratinocyte apoptosis and cutaneous prostaglandin release, while miliaria arises from occlusion of eccrine sweat ducts in hot, humid conditions.
self_care: Apply cold, damp compresses to sunburnt skin for 15 minutes several times daily.
Moisturize frequently with pure aloe vera gel or calamine lotion.
Stay in cool, air-conditioned, well-ventilated spaces and drink plenty of water.
Wear loose, soft cotton clothing; avoid tight friction against the burned areas.

otc_regimen.molecule: Pure Aloe Vera Gel 99% + Calamine Lotion 15%
otc_regimen.dosage: Apply generously over the affected skin areas
otc_regimen.duration: Until erythema and tenderness resolve (3 to 5 days)

otc_regimen.dosage: 1 tablet every 8 hours PRN for skin tenderness

red_flags: Extensive blister formation covering more than 20% of the body surface area
High fever, chills, dizziness, confusion, or severe heat exhaustion symptoms
Secondary bacterial superinfection with purulent crusts or red streaking
Severe facial swelling
solar_erythema_sunburn.referral: Consult a dermatologist or urgent care clinic if blistering is extensive, covers the face, or if signs of systemic toxicity develop.
